text:
Data Controller
Elena Cossu, Max Weber Fellow, Robert Schuman Centre for Advanced Studies, European University Institute (EUI), Via delle Fontanelle 19, 50014 San Domenico di Fiesole (FI), Italy.
Contact: elena.cossu@eui.eu

title: Privacy Notice
section: Purpose and Legal Basis of Processing
text:
Purpose and Legal Basis of Processing
This research project analyses publicly available social media communications (Twitter/X posts) of political parties and political figures across seven European countries (Austria, Czechia, France, Hungary, Italy, Poland, United Kingdom), covering the period 2006–2023. The purpose is to study patterns of illiberal and far-right political communication using computational methods.
The legal basis for processing is Article 6(1)(e) GDPR — processing in the public interest and for scientific research purposes — in accordance with EUI Data Protection Policy (President’s Decision No. 10/2019) and Recital 157 GDPR on scientific research.

title: Privacy Notice
text:
Categories of Data Processed
Publicly available posts from official accounts of political parties and their leaders and representatives while in official capacity. No private communications, direct messages, or data from non-public accounts have been collected.

title: Privacy Notice
text:
Data Subjects

Political parties as organizations
Elected officials and party leaders acting in their official public capacity
Any other individuals identifiable through the content of analysed posts

title: Privacy Notice
text:
Notification and Exemption
Given the large number of data subjects across seven countries, individual notification is not feasible without compromising the scientific integrity of the research. This notice therefore fulfils the transparency obligation under Art. 14 GDPR by means of public disclosure, invoking the exemption provided by Art. 14(5)(b) GDPR (disproportionate effort), consistent with Recital 157 GDPR on scientific research.

title: Privacy Notice
text:
Data Storage and Security
Data is stored on EUI secure server infrastructure and Sciences Po Paris institutional platforms with EU data residency. Access is restricted to project team members. All files containing identifiable information are encrypted and password-protected. No data is shared via unsecured channels.

title: Privacy Notice
text:
Retention Period
Raw data will be retained for the duration of the project and for a maximum of five years following its conclusion, in line with standard academic data retention practices.

title: Privacy Notice
text:
Your Rights
As a data subject you have the right to:

(a) verify what data is processed about you;
(b) request rectification of factually incorrect data;
(c) request removal of your data if your account has subsequently been made private.

Requests can be submitted to elena.cossu@eui.eu. You will receive a response within 30 working days.
You may also address remarks to the EUI Data Protection Officer at: Data_Protection_Officer@EUI.eu

title: Research
text: This project’s goal is to elaborate on how we can use a large corpus of text data together with machine learning to operationalise a multi-faceted and complex concept such as illiberalism. First, we elaborate on the different machine learning and Natural Language Processing methodologies available for such purpose. We present a review of methodologies that could be useful to conceptualise illiberalism using text data, and how we are planning to build a model using these methodologies. We then elaborate on potential sources of data and how to access them. We also report on how to link different resources and why manifestos, parliamentary speeches, and social media data are the best potential fit. Third, we elaborate on the conceptualisation of illiberalism and on the process we used to label the data. In the end we use a deep learning model to classify texts associated with illiberalism. We specifically will use a MdBERTa multilingual model trained on our whole corpus to classify texts characterised by illiberalism. We show the results of the model and we use the newly labelled text to build a ‘map of illiberalisms’. Our final goal is to understand the salient characteristics of texts containing illiberalism and to create a map that highlights the distinctive ideological features of illiberalism and neo-authoritarian values versus liberal democratic values. We do so by using Word Embeddings to place all the newly labelled texts on a relevant scale. This map built on our MdBERTa model gives us the options to explore new underlying dynamics and potential new associations of words and topics to illiberalism.

title: Research
section: Project 2 - Conceptualising Policies Linked to Populist Rhetoric in Europe and Measuring Their Effects in Hungary
text:
Project 2 - Conceptualising Policies Linked to Populist Rhetoric in Europe and Measuring Their Effects in Hungary
This project aims at defining and measuring populism in terms of political and economic practices in Europe. In fact, even if populism is a fundamentally an anti-pluralist phenomenon, it manifests in Europe with specific nuances compared to other parts of the world. Governments characterised by populist rhetoric in Europe are often associated to illiberalism. In this sense, this works tries to look at (i) how we can conceptualise populism in relation to its more applied literature, (ii) how we can conceptualize its practices in Europe, and (iii) what are its economic consequences in a representative case such as the Hungarian one.

Welcome! I am a Max Weber Fellow at the EUI, using computational social science to study democratic backsliding in Europe.
My current research applies machine learning to classify illiberalism in political texts. Previously, I used experiments and quasi-experiments to evaluate the impact of policies across Europe.
I’m always open to explire possible collaborations-let’s connect! you can reach me at: elena.cossu@sciencespo.fr.
